title: Presenting your design
idea: A design presentation is a short, guided tour: the problem, the classes that solve it, one use case traced end to end, and the trade-offs you chose.
points: Open with the requirements in one breath, so everyone judges the same problem.
Show the class diagram, then trace one use case through real method calls.
Name each trade-off and the alternative you rejected, with the reason.
Answer "what if" questions by pointing at the class that would change.

messages.label: book(room, slot)
messages.note: Start from the user's action. The audience follows one request, not the whole diagram at once.

messages.label: forRoom(roomId)
messages.note: The service asks the repository for existing bookings. Say why storage sits behind its own class.

messages.label: conflicts(slot, existing)
messages.note: The overlap rule lives in a strategy. This is where you defend the Open/closed (OCP) choice.

messages.label: save(booking)
messages.note: Only a clash-free booking is stored. Point out that no double booking is enforced here.

messages.label: onBooked(booking)
messages.note: Notification is a separate job. Mention you could swap email for chat without touching the service.

messages.label: Booking
messages.note: End where you started: the employee gets a booking. Then invite questions.

takeaway: Tell one story: problem, classes, one traced flow, then trade-offs.

starters: How long should a design walkthrough take?
How do I answer a question I did not plan for?
Should I show code or only diagrams when presenting?
